title: Song of Solomon 3
paragraphs: ¹ All night long on my bed I looked for him whom I love with all my heart; I looked for him but did not find him. ² "I will get up now and go about the city, through its streets and squares; I will search for him whom I love." I looked for him but did not find him. ³ The watchmen going through the city found me, and I asked, "Have you seen him whom I love?" ⁴ Scarcely had I passed them when I found him whom I love. I held him and would not let him go until I had brought him to my mother's house, into the room where I was conceived. ⁵ I charge you, O daughters of Jerusalem, by the gazelles and the does of the field — do not stir up or awaken love until it is ready.

⁶ Who is this rising from the wilderness like pillars of smoke, perfumed with myrrh and frankincense, with every kind of fragrant spice? ⁷ Look — it is Solomon's carriage, surrounded by sixty valiant warriors, the mightiest men of Israel. ⁸ They are all armed with swords, all skilled in battle; each has his sword at his side, ready for the terrors of the night. ⁹ King Solomon made himself a carriage from the wood of Lebanon. ¹⁰ He made its posts of silver, its seat of gold, its canopy of purple; its interior lovingly crafted by the daughters of Jerusalem.
¹¹ Come out, O daughters of Zion, and look at King Solomon wearing the crown his mother placed on his head on the day of his wedding — the day his heart was filled with joy.
